children.text: After a password reset, the sign-in handler looks up the old reset token, finds it deleted, and throws instead of continuing. Anyone who resets a password cannot sign in until their session cookie is cleared.
Based on: reproduced on staging; the stack trace ends in the reset-token lookup
1. Treat a missing reset token as already used, and continue sign-in.
2. Add a test that signs in immediately after a reset.
3. Deploy to production and watch the sign-in error rate.
Sign-in service, every user signing in
Yes, by redeploying the previous build

children.text: Why not just restart the sign-in service? Would that clear it?
No. The error is in the code path, not in cached state, so it would come back on the next password reset. A restart would only sign everyone out.
Fine. Mention the cookie workaround in the reply to Sam.
Done. I added one sentence about clearing cookies to the draft. The plan itself is unchanged.
